BLOCKER: config/residency-policy.json begins with a UTF-8 BOM; Go's json.Unmarshal rejects it, so LoadRegionPolicy always errors and the region-aware restore guard (AC) cannot run as shipped.

FullRestore/TenantRestore strip the password from the DSN (dsnEnv) but pass PGPASSWORD only to pg_restore; psql and pg_dump run via run()/CommandContext with no Env, so drill commands fail authentication unless the cluster uses trust auth.
AC unmet: the full drill never verifies schema_migrations, performs row counts only (no per-table checksums), and DrillReport records no archive age (RPO).

AC test coverage unmet: no tests for drill verification math (RTO/isolation/checksum) and none for the reconcile repair guard; only PITR parsing, region routing, Classify, and scratch guard are tested.
MAJOR: Classify filters object keys by --prefix but not metadata rows, so with a prefix every out-of-prefix ref is reported Missing and --repair will DELETE those artifact/memory rows (data-loss path).
dsnEnv password extraction uses the first '@' in the authority; a password containing '@' silently falls back to embedding the secret in psql/pg_dump argv (visible via process listing).

Region guard fails open for unmapped tenants: shipped policy has empty "cells" with default "local", so any unknown tenant is treated as home=local and a matching target bypasses residency, contradicting the registry's "fail closed when absent" contract.
The --allow-cross-region reason is accepted but never persisted or audited; no audit trail for a data-residency override.

Archiver age is reported but never evaluated against any threshold: a stalled archiver (failed_count=0, last_archived weeks ago) still yields OK=true, so the readiness check is not actionable for RPO.
TenantRestore never drops the scratch database on success or failure (no defer cleanup), unlike FullRestore; scratch DBs accumulate in the target cluster.
Isolation check uses `tenant_id <> $1`, which excludes NULL tenant_id rows, so cross-tenant/NULL leakage in scratch is undetected.
Full drill materializes the entire pg_dump in memory via .Output(); this does not scale to production-sized databases.
MINOR: Default --scratch value "pf_backup_drill" never satisfies GuardScratch's required "pf_scratch_" prefix, so the default invocation always fails.
--region-policy default path "config/residency-policy.json" is CWD-relative; the binary breaks when run outside the repo root.
TenantRestore ignores --rto-seconds (records elapsed time but no budget comparison), unlike FullRestore.
pg_stat_archiver query error is discarded (`_ =`), so archiver stats can silently be absent from the report.
REVIEW-GATES-LIFECYCLE.md new "Binding order" paragraph contains mojibake arrows ("? Gate 1.5"), corrupting the documented gate sequence.

Process-gate changes (gate0_check relaxation, gate2_completion_check hard-gating, go_modules_check logic) are bundled into a feature item, mixing delivery process changes with product code in one reviewable diff.
NIT: go.mod import block mixes stdlib "time" with third-party imports; goimports grouping convention not followed.
Classify keys the rows map by ref only, collapsing duplicate object_ref values across artifacts/memory.
--repair flag help says "delete metadata rows whose object is missing" while the AC/registry call these "orphaned METADATA rows" — terminology drift between spec and tool.
DrillReport.Elapsed serializes as raw nanoseconds while RTOSeconds duplicates it in the JSON output.
SUMMARY: Solid structure (Go package, guarded destructive ops, explicit exit codes), but the item does not meet its ACs: no schema_migrations/checksum/RPO recording, missing drill/repair tests, and the shipped residency policy is unparseable (BOM), so the region guard cannot run.
Top risks: a --prefix + --repair combination can delete valid metadata rows, auth handling likely breaks the drills in real environments, and residency defaults fail open for unmapped tenants.
Recommend blocking merge until AC deltas, the BOM/DSN env issues, and the Classify prefix/repair data-loss path are resolved.
